grammarTopics.title: Comparison of adjectives (Steigerung der Adjektive)
grammarTopics.explanation: Einsilbige Adjektive und zweisilbige auf -y bekommen -er (Komparativ) und -est (Superlativ): fast – faster – the fastest. Fast alle anderen zweisilbigen und alle längeren Adjektive bekommen more/most: interesting – more interesting – the most interesting. Schreibregeln: Endkonsonant nach kurzem Vokal verdoppeln (big – bigger), stummes -e fällt weg (nice – nicer), y → i (easy – easier). Unregelmäßig: good – better – the best, bad – worse – the worst.
examples: Do you feel more confident now?
It was easier than I thought.
For me it was the most exciting event of the year.
Your Aunt Amy is the best teacher in the world!
The wave became bigger and bigger.

grammarTopics.title: Comparisons with adjectives (as … as, than)
grammarTopics.explanation: Gleich: as + Grundform + as („genauso … wie"). Verschieden: not as + Grundform + as („nicht so … wie") oder Komparativ + than („…er als"). Mit less + Grundform + than sagst du „weniger … als". Nicht verwechseln: than = als, then = dann.
examples: The River Severn is as long as the River Neckar.
Wales isn't as big as England.
Wales is bigger than Northern Ireland.
Is climbing more dangerous than mountainboarding?
Is climbing less dangerous than mountainboarding?

grammarTopics.title: Defining relative clauses (who, which, that, whose; contact clauses)
grammarTopics.explanation: Notwendige Relativsätze beschreiben ein Nomen genauer. who → Personen, which → Sachen, that → Personen oder Sachen, whose → Besitz (dessen/deren). Vor notwendigen Relativsätzen steht KEIN Komma. Ist das Relativpronomen Subjekt, darf es nie wegfallen. Ist es Objekt (danach folgt ein neues Subjekt), kann es wegfallen – das nennt man contact clause. Präpositionen bleiben meist am Ende: the song (which) we talked about.
examples: My presentation is about the people who/that made Florida.
Do you know the famous film which/that presents a Cuban music project?
That's the man whose film became famous.
Gloria Estefan is a singer (who/that) we talked about in Music class.
commonMistakes: Komma vor dem Relativsatz wie im Deutschen
Relativpronomen weglassen, obwohl es Subjekt ist: „a musician came from Cuba"

conversationScenarios.title: Mein Club
conversationScenarios.situation: Du stellst auf dem „club market" deinen Schulclub vor und willst ein neues Mitglied gewinnen. Die neue Schülerin stellt kritische Fragen.
conversationScenarios.openingLine: Hello! I'm new at this school and I'm looking for a club. Why should I join your club and not the Drama Club?
phrases: Our club is more exciting than …
It's the best club for people who …

n1.npcLine: Hello! I'm new at this school and I'm looking for a club. Why should I join your club and not the Drama Club?

choices.text: Our club is more exciting than the Drama Club! We go on trips and play lots of games.

choices.feedback: Ein Anfang! Mit einem Vergleich überzeugst du mehr: Our club is more exciting than …

choices.text: Our club is more good than the Drama Club.

n2.npcLine: Hmm. Who can join your club?

choices.text: It's the best club for people who like music and dancing.
choices.feedback: Super – Superlativ und Relativsatz mit who!
Gut! Mit Relativsatz klingt es besser: It's for everybody who likes …

choices.text: It's for people which like music.
choices.feedback: Für Personen nimmst du who (oder that), nicht which.

n3.npcLine: Is it expensive? I think the Drama Club is cheaper.

choices.text: No, it isn't. Our club is as cheap as the Drama Club – it only costs £2 a month.
choices.feedback: Perfekt – as cheap as für „genauso billig wie".
Gut! Mit Vergleich: It's as cheap as the Drama Club.

choices.text: Our club is cheaper then the Drama Club.
choices.feedback: Als = than, nicht then: cheaper than.

n4.npcLine: OK, that sounds interesting. When do you meet?

choices.text: We meet every Tuesday after school in the room which is next to the library.

choices.feedback: Richtig! Etwas genauer: We meet every Tuesday after school.

n5.npcLine: Great! I think I'm going to join your club. Thanks!
